evidence.text: Q3 is HEMANGEOL's first full quarter, after only May-June in Q2. The 10-Q says revenue is recognised as product ships against patient orders, so Q2 carried no channel fill. Q2 revenue rose $13.3M sequentially ($24.3M to $37.6M, of which $2.9M was ex-US INCRELEX), which implies HEMANGEOL ran at ~$5.5-6.5M a month by June. Management puts net price at $8-10k per patient on ~8,000 patients a year (~$64-80M annualised). A full quarter of that on a ~$23-25M US base points to ~$43-45M Q3 revenue against the $42.2M consensus, a 2-6% beat.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have been bought. Q2 2026 printed $37.6M against ~$27.2M consensus with a raise and the stock rose +44.3%. Q1 2026 ($24.3M) moved +1.0%. Q3 2025 had revenue above estimates but a gross margin drop to 45% and a payer-mix comment, and the stock fell -11.7%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The consensus of $42.2M is only ~12% above Q2 even though Q3 has 3 HEMANGEOL months against 2. The preview itself says it has no HEMANGEOL run-rate. If the full-quarter arithmetic were priced, consensus would sit at $44M+ and the stock would not be sitting at its post-earnings low ($48.36 low, $49.28 spot).
evidence.independence: Draws on several documents. Net price and patient count come from Q2 call summaries (https://www.stocktaper.com/earningsCallSummary/ETON/2026/Q2, snippet; page returned 429). HEMANGEOL had only $11.7M of 2025 sales (IQVIA) under Pierre Fabre (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1710340/000143774926006209/eton20260223c_8k.htm), so the increment comes from Eton's repricing. ASN-001's $3M was expensed and included in adjusted EBITDA guidance. $10M is ~6-7 points of FY EBITDA margin, which pressures any raise to the >=35% margin guide. If it were priced, Q4 EPS estimates would have been cut after 10-14; consensus Q3 EPS is $0.34 and no revisions were found. Financing question: the money buys a 2027 launch into a >$450M seizure-rescue market, funded from operating cash flow. That is not distress, so this is a small margin-guide negative only.

evidence.text: On 26 Oct 2026 Innodata reportedly let go of nearly 550 staff in India, about 5% of its 10,107 year-end headcount, plus an uncounted number of raters, QA, team leads and managers in the Philippines. The termination emails cite a 'ramp-down of the business assignment'. The company has not commented. Its two largest customers were 71% of Q2 revenue (37% and 34%). The release is management's first chance to say whether this touches the 40%+ FY guide, which needs Q4 near $85M, and the cut most plausibly lands in Q4, since Q3 closed on 30 Sep. Netted against it: in August management said large potential programs from new and existing customers were excluded from the guide, that it expected most to be won, and that it would add them once scope was final. A CEO change on 30 Sep (Singhal in, Abuhoff to executive chairman) makes this the new CEO's first guide, which raises the odds of a reset.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is the line this name trades on. The May 2026 raise from 35%+ to 40%+ with a ~$51M Big Tech program went +86.0%. The Feb 2026 first guide of 35%+ went -7.17%. The June 2026 standalone reaffirmation went -6.85%. The Aug 2026 reaffirmation with a 7% revenue beat went -4.81%. Reaffirmations have been sold; raises have been bought hard.
evidence.why_not_priced: The fact itself is fully priced as a headline: -25% on 27 Oct and a further -16% since. What is not priced is its size. Taken pro rata, 550 of 10,107 staff is roughly 5% of revenue, about $4-5M a quarter. The ~$1.4bn to ~$1.3bn market cap has lost about $700M since 26 Oct, which prices something closer to losing the whole of one large customer. If the market had a number, the straddle would not be at 303% IV with a 46% spread, and the stock would not have fallen 12.5% today on no identified news.
evidence.independence: HRKatha (https://www.hrkatha.com/news/layoff/innodata-layoffs-hit-india-and-the-philippines/, 2026-10-28) separately reports the Philippines cuts tied to 'declining service volumes from a major client project'. Both ultimately rest on India Today's reading of the termination email. The offsetting side, unbooked large programs, comes from the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000903651/000110465926092010/tm2621499d1_ex99-1.htm, 2026-08-06). Concentration and the CEO change come from the same release.

evidence.text: The Q2 10-Q shows advances from customers 'for unfulfilled obligations' of $67.0M at 30 Jun 2026, against $1.8M at 31 Dec 2025, plus $61.8M of incurred but unpaid project costs. A customer prepaid about three quarters of a quarter's revenue for work not yet delivered at the start of Q3. This underpins the Q3 revenue bar of $84.7M, which sits about 8% below Q2's $92.1M.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have not been paid for lately. Q2 2026 beat by about 7% and the stock went -4.81%. Q1 2026 beat by a wide margin with a raise and went +86%, but that move was the guide.
evidence.why_not_priced: The figure sits in the 10-Q notes, not in the press release. In the Q2 call it was only called 'customer prepayments, which are a pass-through'. The previews quote consensus and the layoffs, not the advance balance. If the market read the advance as funded Q3 to Q4 work, a Q3 at or above $85M would not be in question, and today's selling into the print suggests it is. Caveat that sizes this down: pass-through revenue is low-margin, and some of the advance may already have been earned in Q3, which consensus partly reflects. Management also said in August that a sequential decline was 'certainly possible'.
evidence.independence: Q2 call transcript, CFO Chauhan on 'customer prepayments, which are a pass-through' and Abuhoff saying a Q3/Q4 sequential decline is 'certainly possible' (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2942769). Same company and same period, so this is partly the same document set.
